organizations.What they build: ETH incubation/funding program helps eligible students and researchers convert research into spin-offs through funding, coaching and infrastructure. ETH Foundation documents robotics alumni including ANYbotics and Tethys; not a general student-association grant.
organizations.Warm contact path: Ask program staff for a robotics alumni speaker; 42AI members without ETH affiliation should not assume eligibility.
organizations._relationship_reason: Robotics founder introductions and a commercialization talk are realistic; direct fellowship funding is not.

organizations.What they build: Philanthropic Swiss science-to-startup support initiative operated by Venturelab, with Schlieren and Lausanne contacts. Its portfolio documents autonomous underwater robotics company Tethys.
organizations.Warm contact path: info@venturekick.ch; ask for a robotics founder introduction or public entrepreneurship session rather than an association grant.
organizations._relationship_reason: Useful path into early-stage robotics founders; program qualification requires a suitable Swiss research-based venture.

organizations.What they build: Student-run entrepreneurship club offering speakers, startup networking and programs including InCube and Boost. General ecosystem connector, not a dedicated robotics lab or another name for ETH Robotics Club.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public club contact; propose a peer event with ETH robotics students and a 42AI demonstration.
organizations._relationship_reason: Student-to-student introductions are more achievable than asking investors cold for sponsorship.

organizations.What they build: Makerspace offering fabrication, 3D printing, electronics and CNC workshops. Live site advertises 2026 maker activities; distinct from the Bitwäscherei collective.
organizations.Warm contact path: Use public workshop/visitor channels; arrange safety induction and machine access before a group visit.
organizations._relationship_reason: Hands-on fabrication support directly addresses 42AI's weak mechanics/electronics background.

organizations.What they build: Venture investor with industrial-tech/robotics exposure: official portfolio lists autonomous inventory-drone company Verity, invested since 2020. Former investiere branding should not become a second row.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public fund contact; propose a Swiss robotics commercialization talk and ask about a portfolio founder introduction.
organizations._relationship_reason: A mentor or portfolio introduction is plausible; venture funding is for companies, not a 15-student club.

organizations.What they build: Cantonal bank investing in Swiss technology ventures. Venturelab's October 2025 Tethys financing announcement names it among participants in a EUR 3.5M pre-seed round.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public startup-finance channel; request an educational founder-financing talk. No existing warm introduction.
organizations._relationship_reason: A local robotics-investor connection is useful, but Swiss financing eligibility and association sponsorship are unknown.

organizations.What they build: Engineering education program where teams design and build prototypes over fifth/sixth semesters, including robotics and medical/mobility systems; results presented at Focus Rollout. Program row, not a duplicate of each participating club or RSL.
organizations.Warm contact path: Ask the department's public education/event contact for a robotics focus-team exchange or public rollout visit.
organizations._relationship_reason: A strong reference for structuring 42AI's three project teams; external enrolment and facilities access are not assumed.

organizations.What they build: Builds collaborative arms and mobile manipulators including Lio and Sola for care, research and laboratory workflows. Official contact address is Rohrstrasse 36, Glattbrugg.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public company contact; propose a manipulation/teleoperation engineering talk with a small SO-101 demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: Directly relevant to applied manipulation and human interaction; commercial hardware loan availability is unknown.

organizations.What they build: Laboratory automation company. Fluent workstations combine pipetting robotic arms with gripper arms for moving plates and labware; this is tangible robotics, not just diagnostic software.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public automation/application contact; request a lab-automation engineering talk or a nonclinical workflow case study.
organizations._relationship_reason: Robotic workflow planning and repeatability are useful learning topics; no clinical access or equipment donation is implied.

organizations.What they build: Dynamic measurement company supplying force, torque, pressure and acceleration sensors. 9306A measures six-axis forces/moments; relevant to contact measurement and robot testing, not an entire robot platform.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public technical contact for an educational force-measurement session; ask for application advice before hardware support.
organizations._relationship_reason: Force-sensing literacy is relevant to contact-rich learning; industrial sensors may exceed a low-cost lab budget.

organizations.What they build: Elios 3 collision-tolerant confined-space inspection drones reduce human entry into hazardous assets; official site also lists ultrasonic-testing payload and tether power options. Funding stage: unknown.
organizations.Warm contact path: info@flyability.com; request an indoor-inspection/perception engineering talk, not unsupervised industrial flight access.
organizations._relationship_reason: A practical autonomy/sensing case study; sharing a student demo is a better first ask than a drone donation.

organizations.What they build: ARA620 ultra-high-precision sprayer uses AI to distinguish plants and target treatment. It is a tractor-mounted precision implement, not a claim that all current products are autonomous weeding vehicles. Funding stage: unknown.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public company contact; propose an agricultural computer-vision discussion or dataset evaluation exercise.
organizations._relationship_reason: Software-strong students can explore plant perception offline; agricultural machinery access is not required.

organizations.What they build: DEXTER robotic surgery system supports minimally invasive procedures while fitting existing operating-room workflows and instrument preferences. Funding stage: unknown.
organizations.Warm contact path: info@distalmotion.com; ask for an educational surgical-robotics/systems-safety talk, without requesting patient or operating-room access.
organizations._relationship_reason: Useful teleoperation and validation lessons; clinical deployment is outside 42AI's student project scope.

organizations.What they build: Emovo Clinic is a robotic hand exoskeleton; Emovo Research offers research-only hand exoskeletons with one to five active fingers, sensing and software APIs. Distinguishes certified clinical and noncertified research devices. Funding stage: unknown.
organizations.Warm contact path: hello@emovocare.com; request a research API or assistive-manipulation seminar, not clinical testing.
organizations._relationship_reason: An unusually concrete software/physical-interface bridge; hardware affordability and lending need confirmation.

organizations.What they build: Develops personal lower-limb exoskeletons to help people with spinal cord injuries stand and walk; emphasizes lightweight user-centered mobility. Funding stage: unknown.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public company contact for an assistive-robotics design talk. No patient trials or unsupervised exoskeleton use proposed.
organizations._relationship_reason: Human-centered mechanics and safety are valuable complements to software skills; direct hardware access is not assumed.

organizations.Organization: EPFL Learning Algorithms and Systems Laboratory (LASA)
organizations.What they build: Aude Billard's laboratory studies teaching robots dexterous skills from human demonstrations and adaptive/reactive control under obstacles or perturbations.
organizations.Warm contact path: No established warm introduction. Use the official lab/center contact to propose a short student technical exchange, sharing a LeRobot/SO-101 demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: Very strong fit to learning from demonstrations; start with an open paper/code reading discussion rather than asking for formal supervision.

organizations.Organization: EPFL Computational Robot Design & Fabrication Lab (CREATE)
organizations.What they build: Josie Hughes's laboratory develops computational design and fabrication for sensorized, multi-material robots, manipulation and robot-driven physical experimentation.
organizations.Warm contact path: No established warm introduction. Use the official lab/center contact to propose a short student technical exchange, sharing a LeRobot/SO-101 demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: A scoped engineering talk, student introduction or dataset/simulation exercise is realistic; equipment access and funded collaboration require separate agreement.

organizations.What they build: Dario Floreano's group studies bio-inspired aerial, wearable and soft robotics, including drone learning/control and resilient robot design.
organizations.Warm contact path: No established warm introduction. Use the official lab/center contact to propose a short student technical exchange, sharing a LeRobot/SO-101 demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: A scoped engineering talk, student introduction or dataset/simulation exercise is realistic; equipment access and funded collaboration require separate agreement.

organizations.What they build: Jamie Paik's laboratory develops reconfigurable, origami and soft robots, novel actuation and wearable interfaces; projects include Tribot, Mori and Mori3.
organizations.Warm contact path: No established warm introduction. Use the official lab/center contact to propose a short student technical exchange, sharing a LeRobot/SO-101 demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: A scoped engineering talk, student introduction or dataset/simulation exercise is realistic; equipment access and funded collaboration require separate agreement.

organizations.What they build: Auke Ijspeert's lab studies locomotion, sensorimotor coordination and learning through neuromechanical simulation, amphibious/legged robots and rehabilitation exoskeletons.
organizations.Warm contact path: No established warm introduction. Use the official lab/center contact to propose a short student technical exchange, sharing a LeRobot/SO-101 demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: A scoped engineering talk, student introduction or dataset/simulation exercise is realistic; equipment access and funded collaboration require separate agreement.

organizations.What they build: Develops neurotechnologies to restore sensorimotor function. Robotics-relevant work includes sensory prosthetics and cognitive control of an extra robotic arm; not every neuroengineering project is a robot.
organizations.Warm contact path: No established warm introduction. Use the official lab/center contact to propose a short student technical exchange, sharing a LeRobot/SO-101 demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: A scoped engineering talk, student introduction or dataset/simulation exercise is realistic; equipment access and funded collaboration require separate agreement.

organizations.What they build: Herbert Shea's laboratory develops compliant actuators, stretchable sensors, soft transducers and wearable haptic displays for applications including soft robotics and dexterous manipulation. Located at EPFL's Neuchâtel site, not Lausanne.
organizations.Warm contact path: No established warm introduction. Use the official lab/center contact to propose a short student technical exchange, sharing a LeRobot/SO-101 demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: A scoped engineering talk, student introduction or dataset/simulation exercise is realistic; equipment access and funded collaboration require separate agreement.

organizations.What they build: Technical university providing robotics education, research laboratories, student MAKE projects and spin-off pathways. Separate lab rows identify practical contacts, not additional universities.
organizations.Warm contact path: No established warm introduction. Use the official robotics education contact to propose a short student technical exchange, sharing a LeRobot/SO-101 demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: A scoped engineering talk, student introduction or dataset/simulation exercise is realistic; equipment access and funded collaboration require separate agreement.

organizations.What they build: Interfaculty center connecting robotics research, education, students, spin-offs and industrial partners across perception, control, learning, medical robotics and design.
organizations.Warm contact path: No established warm introduction. Use the official lab/center contact to propose a short student technical exchange, sharing a LeRobot/SO-101 demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: A scoped engineering talk, student introduction or dataset/simulation exercise is realistic; equipment access and funded collaboration require separate agreement.

organizations.What they build: Student-run EPFL robotics club and makerspace with electronics/mechanical tools, workshops and open sessions. Official page welcomes members from EPFL or other schools; visitor conditions should still be checked.
organizations.Warm contact path: robopoly@epfl.ch; arrange a peer build session or introductory workshop visit, checking external access first.
organizations._relationship_reason: Closest peer-level route to shared build sessions and engineering lessons across software, electronics and mechanics.

organizations.What they build: Student association designs Mars-style rovers and drones for the European Rover Challenge, conducts space-robotics research and teaches robotics through mini-rover projects.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public student-team contact; propose a 42AI rover/perception software exchange with a small demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: Closest peer-level route to shared build sessions and engineering lessons across software, electronics and mechanics.

organizations.What they build: Innovation campus and startup community with coworking/prototyping ecosystem around EPFL; official locations page explicitly includes robotics among represented technologies. Not a stand-alone robotics lab.
organizations.Warm contact path: No established warm introduction. Use the official community/park contact to propose a short student technical exchange, sharing a LeRobot/SO-101 demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: A scoped engineering talk, student introduction or dataset/simulation exercise is realistic; equipment access and funded collaboration require separate agreement.

organizations.What they build: Builds EXRAY underwater inspection robots, LUMA optical underwater communications and DISKDRIVE propulsion; aims to acquire asset-integrity data without conventional tethered interventions. Funding stage: unknown.
organizations.Warm contact path: No established warm introduction. Use the official company contact to propose a short student technical exchange, sharing a LeRobot/SO-101 demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: A scoped engineering talk, student introduction or dataset/simulation exercise is realistic; equipment access and funded collaboration require separate agreement.

organizations.What they build: Supplies Autonomous Navigation Technology (ANT) and integration support for AGVs, autonomous forklifts and AMRs; focuses on natural-feature navigation rather than building every customer vehicle.
organizations.Warm contact path: No established warm introduction. Use the official company contact to propose a short student technical exchange, sharing a LeRobot/SO-101 demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: A scoped engineering talk, student introduction or dataset/simulation exercise is realistic; equipment access and funded collaboration require separate agreement.

organizations.What they build: Develops Webots open-source robot simulator and supplies commercial support, training, consulting and custom robotics simulations. Established simulation publisher, not a new robot-hardware startup.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public Webots repository/community first; sales@cyberbotics.com for scoped training or simulation advice.
organizations._relationship_reason: Simulation is an affordable entry point before hardware; student contributions and a technical talk are realistic.

organizations.What they build: Human-centered robot learning from a few demonstrations and interactions, including manipulation, optimal control, reinforcement learning and physical human-robot collaboration.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public group contact; ask Sylvain Calinon's team for an open-code study discussion and share a small imitation-learning reproduction.
organizations._relationship_reason: One of the closest matches to 42AI's low-data learning wedge; reproducible code is a better first interaction than asking for formal supervision.

organizations.What they build: Applied research/technology-transfer organization developing sensors, intelligent automation and inspection; lab-automation work explicitly combines robotics, imaging, liquid handling and software.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public industry/research contact; request an educational sensor-fusion or laboratory-automation talk with a scoped demo.
organizations._relationship_reason: Practical sensing/integration expertise complements software students; paid industrial R&D is not assumed accessible to a club.

organizations.What they build: Joint USI-SUPSI institute's autonomous robotics area studies self-supervised perception, flying/ground robots, industrial robotics and energy-efficient embedded AI.
organizations.Warm contact path: Alessandro Giusti's public SUPSI research contact; propose reproducing an open robotic-perception baseline.
organizations._relationship_reason: Low-data perception and embedded deployment can be explored without expensive robot hardware.

organizations.What they build: Applied research lab for collaborative, industrial and mobile robotics, image processing and mechatronics. Advertises practical demonstrations and a robot park including Panda, UR3, P-Rob and Meca500.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public laboratory contacts Gabriel Gruener / Raphael Rätz; ask for an educational visit or collaborative-robot safety discussion.
organizations._relationship_reason: Explicit lab visits and a diverse robot park make this a practical bridge from SO-101 experiments to industrial manipulation.

organizations.What they build: Applied institute combining robotics, mechatronics and industrial electronics. Robotics expertise includes ROS/ROS 2, mobile manipulation, safety and simulation with RoboDK.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public iAi direction/contact; propose a French-language ROS 2 and manipulation software exchange.
organizations._relationship_reason: French-speaking applied robotics team is a plausible mentor and integration partner; funded projects require a separate agreement.

organizations.What they build: Builds and tests automated machines for manufacturing, mobility, space and medical partners. Teaching/research robot cells include ABB IRB1200, YuMi and KUKA iiwa with vision and force sensing.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public robotics laboratory contacts Michel Lauria / Jeremy Olivier; request a French-language student exchange or simulation session.
organizations._relationship_reason: Accessible applied-robotics vocabulary and collaborative cells fit an engineering/safety learning visit.

organizations.What they build: Applied institute for modern control, industrial/building automation and mechatronics. Its robotics laboratory supports prototyping, student projects and external access by arrangement; work includes AI weed control.
organizations.Warm contact path: Robot-lab contact Wolfgang Fischer; ask for a student demonstration exchange, checking access and fees first.
organizations._relationship_reason: Practical control/automation mentoring is valuable; located in Aargau, not Basel city despite FHNW's regional footprint.

organizations.What they build: Competence Center Mechanical Systems robotics activity develops industrial automation and mobile robots for changing environments, including human-facing tasks, agricultural and care applications.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public competence-center contact on the official robotics page; request a short applied autonomy/robot safety exchange.
organizations._relationship_reason: A practical counterpoint to foundation-model hype; software students can learn how sensing and mechanics constrain deployment.

organizations.Organization: OST Institute for Lab Automation and Mechatronics (ILT)
organizations.What they build: Develops industrial/collaborative robotic solutions, mobile manipulation, lab automation and flexible smart-factory systems.
organizations.Warm contact path: ilt@ost.ch or public institute lead Agathe Koller; request an educational mobile-manipulation case study.
organizations._relationship_reason: Offers concrete integration examples; a scoped software demonstration could earn technical feedback.

organizations.What they build: Swiss industrial automation company building robot linear tracks, modular linear axes/gantries, gearboxes, guideways and integrated automation solutions.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public technical contact; propose a motion-system and automation-design seminar before considering equipment sponsorship.
organizations._relationship_reason: Mechanical motion-system expertise fills a genuine student gap; heavy industrial hardware is not an immediate low-cost lab purchase.

organizations.What they build: Swiss Hamilton operation develops/manufactures laboratory automation products; liquid-handling robot platforms integrate pipetting, monitoring, consumables and devices for repeatable assay workflows. Parent also operates in the US.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public automation/application contact for a nonclinical lab-robot workflow seminar; no established warm introduction.
organizations._relationship_reason: Repeatability and workflow integration provide useful robotics lessons without requiring access to biological samples.

organizations.What they build: Elevator/escalator group using R.I.S.E (Robotic Installation System for Elevators) to drill precise holes and set anchors in elevator shafts. Official historical report describes relieving installers of strenuous repetitive work.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public innovation/media contact; ask for a technical construction-robotics case-study talk, not an active-site visit.
organizations._relationship_reason: Demonstrates a narrow industrial robot task with clear safety/productivity value; useful contrast to general-purpose humanoids.

organizations.What they build: National robotics association launched in 2024, building on the legacy of NCCR Robotics and the Innosuisse-powered Robotics Innovation Booster; connects research, industry and public outreach.
organizations.Warm contact path: contact@swiss-robotics.org; ask for student-friendly events and French-speaking research/industry introductions.
organizations._relationship_reason: High-leverage national entry point; request introductions rather than implying membership or sponsorship is already agreed.

organizations.What they build: Swiss innovation agency funding research-to-market collaboration, startups and innovation programs. Funder classification, not an equity VC; EPFL LASA explicitly lists its Robotics Innovation Booster.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public program information and a Swiss research partner first; ask about eligibility, not a direct grant for a French student club.
organizations._relationship_reason: May enable a later eligible Swiss collaboration; near-term value is understanding partner/program routes.

organizations.Organization: AMLD Intelligence Summit (Applied Machine Learning Days)
organizations.What they build: EPFL-linked applied-AI event. Organizer's February 2026 announcement lists a live physical-intelligence keynote with EPFL/ETH construction, manipulation and legged robots; wider event is not exclusively robotics.
organizations.Warm contact path: Public event organizer channel; inquire about student rates and a small robotics demo or community exchange. Next edition arrangements unknown.
organizations._relationship_reason: A plausible place for software-strong students to meet robotics researchers; do not assume a robot-specific hackathon.

updates_existing.name: Stäubli Robotics France
updates_existing.fact: Parent group is Swiss: Stäubli International AG is headquartered in Pfäffikon (SZ); Swiss robotics service/training is in Horgen and Peseux. Keeping this as an existing-row update rather than duplicating the robotics group.
